title: The Power of the First Impression: How Connected TV Advertising Wins the CTV Boot-Up Moment
summary: Viewers spend 14 minutes browsing the Smart TV home screen before watching. Learn how connected TV advertising wins the first impression at boot-up.
body_markdown:
Viewers now spend an average of[14 minutes looking for something to watch](https://www.nielsen.com/news-center/2025/new-gracenote-report-highlights-impact-of-ineffective-content-discovery-on-consumer-happiness-with-streaming/) , which is more than half a sitcom episode, and nearly one in five eventually give up entirely. All of that searching happens on the Smart TV home screen, well before the first ad break, at a point in the evening when people are deliberate and largely free of advertising.


The first brand to appear in that moment secures an outsized impression as a result, with research across more than 1,500 campaigns revealing that[74% of attention goes to the first ad viewers see](https://www.teads.com/blog/ctv-homescreen-1500-campaigns/3177/) . That gives modern[connected TV advertising](https://www.teads.com/lp/connected-tv-advertising/) a rare kind of opening to anchor awareness. Through direct partnerships with the likes of LG, Samsung, and Google TV, our[CTV HomeScreen placements](https://www.teads.com/blog/what-is-ctv-homescreen/) ensure enterprise brands own the first impression of the evening.


## **What Is the CTV Boot-Up Moment?**


The CTV boot-up moment begins the instant someone switches on a Smart TV and lasts until they choose something to watch, and most of it happens on the TV’s home screen. Far from passive viewers, audiences during this stage are actively engaged: scanning rows of titles, evaluating recommendations, and switching between apps. On a platform like Google TV, that means browsing[more than 400,000 movies and shows from over 10,000 apps](https://www.teads.com/blog/teads-partners-with-google-tv-to-expand-ctv-homescreen-availability-globally/9811/) gathered into one interface.


For Connected TV (CTV) advertising, that makes for a useful combination. The viewer’s eyes are on the screen because choosing something requires it, and very little advertising is competing for them yet, since the show and its ad breaks haven’t started. People can spend[up to 10 minutes browsing before they meet any ad clutter](https://www.teads.com/blog/ctv-homescreen-1500-campaigns/3177/) , and a brand that appears in that window reaches someone who’s already looking.


## **Why CTV HomeScreen Ads Earn More Attention**


CTV ads in a break meet viewers partway through a show they’ve already picked. HomeScreen ads meet them earlier, while they’re still deciding, and the attention data reflects the difference. Our attention measurement with Lumen Research puts CTV HomeScreen campaigns at[around 5,300 Attention Per Mille on average](https://www.teads.com/blog/teads-and-lumen-research-bring-proven-attention-science-to-ctv-for-omnichannel-impact/10475/) , 173% higher than outstream video and 114% higher than YouTube.

In an eye-tracking study with 100 Smart TV viewers, recall followed the attention, with[HomeScreen ads reaching 50% unaided recall and 84% aided recall](https://www.teads.com/blog/new-study-teads-ctv-homescreen-drives-superior-attention-and-brand-impact-across-premium-video-advertising/7660/) , well ahead of the in-stream formats tested alongside them. The lab findings and the campaign-level attention data point the same way, which gives planners good reason to make room for the home screen in their connected TV advertising budgets.


## **Global OEM CTV Partnerships: LG, VIDAA, Samsung, and Google TV**


For connected TV advertising, reaching the boot-up moment largely depends on access to the home screens themselves, and those belong to the companies that build the TVs and their operating systems. Our partnerships cover several of the largest:


1. **LG:** Our[exclusive partnership with LG Ad Solutions](https://marketech-apac.com/teads-lg-ad-solutions-renew-ctv-partnership-to-expand-premium-homescreen-reach-across-apac-europe/) , renewed in 2026, gives advertisers LG HomeScreen inventory across Asia-Pacific and Europe, with more markets planned.


1. **VIDAA:** With an exclusive[multi-year partnership with V (formerly VIDAA)](https://www.teads.com/blog/teads-and-v-make-black-friday-a-homescreen-moment/11754/) , advertisers gain access to hardware-level targeting based on TV screen size and room context, alongside exclusive HomeScreen takeovers during peak retail windows like Black Friday.


1. **Samsung:** Since February 2026,[we’ve partnered with Samsung Ads](https://www.teads.com/blog/teads-and-samsung-ads-to-unlock-next-generation-ctv-homescreen-advertising-across-select-sea-markets-hong-kong-and-taiwan/9880/) to bring Samsung Smart TV home screen display and video ads to advertisers in Malaysia, the Philippines, Thailand, Vietnam, Hong Kong, Taiwan, and Indonesia.


1. **Google TV:** Our Google TV partnership opens up the Masthead, the first visual impression on Google TV devices, in markets including the US, the UK, and Asia-Pacific.


With further partners such as Whale TV, Titan, and TiVo, our HomeScreen inventory now reaches[more than 500 million unique TV devices, and over 4,000 HomeScreen campaigns have run](https://www.teads.com/blog/teads-partners-with-google-tv-to-expand-ctv-homescreen-availability-globally/9811/) since the format launched in 2023. In a standout execution, Michelin partnered with BETC and[Teads Studio to create an immersive 3D HomeScreen](https://www.teads.com/blog/teads-partners-with-google-tv-to-expand-ctv-homescreen-availability-globally/9811/) experience. The placement delivered **+7% brand favorability** , **+8% perception of safety** , and **+6% brand consideration** .

## **Connecting the First Impression to the Rest of the Plan**


The home screen does its best work as part of a wider[omnichannel video strategy](https://www.teads.com/omnichannel/) . Speaking at the Possible conference this year, our CEO David Kostman described it as[one of the best places to drive attention outcomes](https://www.beet.tv/2026/05/your-tv-ads-start-on-the-home-screen-whether-you-like-it-or-not-teads-ceo-david-kostman.html) , and that value grows significantly when the impression connects to everything else a brand runs. A HomeScreen placement can sit alongside CTV InStream breaks,[interactive and shoppable CTV ad formats](https://www.teads.com/blog/connected-tv-ad-formats-explained-homescreen-instream-and-performance/10336/) , and premium digital environments, each reinforcing the same brand platform in whatever order the household meets them, an idea we explored in[our guide to cross-screen connected media](https://www.teads.com/blog/what-is-cross-screen-connected-media-and-why-it-starts-with-connected-tv-advertising/12194/) .


Brand and performance capabilities sit under one roof as well. A connected TV advertising campaign that includes the home screen can be judged on attention and recall, and also on[site visits and other lower-funnel outcomes through CTV Performance](https://www.teads.com/blog/ctv-performance-is-now-generally-available-turning-the-living-room-into-an-outcomes-engine/11159/) , with budget moving between the two as results come in.

Each TV manufacturer runs its own home screen, so for brands that advertise on connected TV in several markets, one route in makes planning far simpler.[Teads Ad Manager brings that supply together as a single connected TV advertising platform](https://www.teads.com/lp/teads-ad-manager) , where HomeScreen inventory from multiple manufacturers sits alongside InStream, CTV Performance, and premium digital.


Advertisers can[plan, execute, and optimize HomeScreen campaigns there](https://www.teads.com/blog/ctv-homescreen-1500-campaigns/3177/) with the same CTV targeting they use on other screens. Lumen attention measurement is available on HomeScreen for managed and self-serve CTV campaigns alike, so CTV measurement covers the quality of the first impression as well as its reach.
